bonuses.requirements: U.S. Personal Savings Rate Falls to 4.2% in September, Lowest Since October 2022HomeFeedNewsU.S. Personal Savings Rate Falls to 4.2% in September, Lowest Since October 2022U.S. Personal Savings Rate Falls to 4.2% in September, Lowest Since October 202210/31 20:45On November 1, The Kobeissi Letter reported that the U.S. personal savings rate declined by 0.2 percentage points to 4.2% in September, marking the lowest level since October 2022. Since January 2024, the personal savings rate has decreased by a total of 3.4 percentage points. Currently, the savings rate is significantly below the pre-pandemic average of 6.2% over the past five years. Meanwhile, personal income in the U.S. grew by 4.1% year-on-year in September, the second-lowest growth rate since April 2022. During the same period, personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased by 6.3% year-on-year, the second-highest year-on-year increase since December 2024. In other words, the growth rate of consumer spending continues to outpace income growth, further squeezing household savings and increasing reliance on borrowing. To address this, DeepSeek proposes the "Super-agent," a continuous entity that spans sessions, advances multiple tasks concurrently without interference, and exhibits four traits: continuous, efficient, proactive, and persistent. The architecture comprises five modules. First, a two-layer design: a resident Router layer handles human interaction, global coordination, and memory (using a lighter model, with batching of queued triggers during inference), while context-isolated Worker sessions execute tasks in parallel with the strongest models and report back through the Router; sessions become an implementation detail rather than a user burden. Second, event-driven operation: semi-structured environment events ("Triggers") replace typed prompts, filtered via a fast/slow path of deterministic program rules plus LLM semantic judgment; subscription and direct-pass routing send thread events straight to subscribed Workers; Inline & Spill context management with chain-of-recall IDs lets models retrieve context on demand; and speculative execution enables proactive background work. Vercel stated that 10 of the affected domains are associated with its platform. Earlier reports indicated that late Friday, hackers breached over a dozen DeFi websites, including Flap, Kintsu, Pickle Finance, and Origami Finance, and exploited these sites to drain visitors' cryptocurrency wallets. According to registration records obtained by The Block, all 12 hijacked domains were registered through Name.com, with 10 of them being suspended at the registrar level on Saturday morning.
